context: Request: the most recent closed M&A deal with disclosure schedules to use as a template. The log header names no matters; the criteria require 1006-00008 (Crestline Packaging APA signed June 16, 2025, closed August 15, 2025) and its disclosure-schedules.docx, and nothing else as qualifying.

stages.note: Whole-store glob in parallel with a folder-name listing capped at 80 lines and a file count.

stages.stage: List matter folders
stages.note: Lists all matter folders with file counts; the review notes the display was cut after about a third of the folders.

stages.stage: List matter folders
stages.note: Attempt 2: same listing split into three number ranges.

stages.stage: List matter folders
stages.note: Attempt 3: per-prefix folder counts and first/last names; the review says goal reached.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: Path script for schedule, purchase-agreement, merger and closing words fails once, then lists 231 matters (about 199K chars); the review flags that candidates were then named by highest matter number.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: Attempt 2: intersects schedule-file and agreement-file names, 28 matters; the review flags the intersection filter and ranking by matter number.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads agreements, schedules, certificates and checklists of five high-numbered matters, then eight more reads; one guessed path fails. The review lists surfaced matters never opened.

stages.stage: List files in candidate matters
stages.note: Lists all files of nine high-numbered candidate matters.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: List files in candidate matters. Reads five closing emails, memos and drafts from the listed matters; the review flags about 60 surfaced matters never listed or opened.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Extraction script over the 35 matters with schedule-named files for closing-status and date phrases (about 90K chars); the review flags the schedule-name restriction and candidates judged from snippets.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: declared: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth. Reads cover pages of agreements, schedules and closing certificates from four candidates to compare closing dates; one guessed path fails; a stage_start for writing is refused while this stage is open.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes one matter closed in mid-2025 as the most recent deal with schedules, with older backups and exclusions; the review flags the hedged recency claim and comparison candidates that could inflate the answer.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response, checks cited paths, replaces one missing path with an existing letter.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 2: re-reads the letter, the agreement and the closing certificate; no edits.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

runs.sequence: List files in the document store → List matter folders → Search file names for request keywords → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → List files in candidate matters → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Scan document text with an extraction script → Screen candidate matters by reading documents → Write the response → Check or revise the response → Finish the run
runs.failure_point: It picked candidates by highest matter number, and when a later scan showed more closed deals it opened them but not the matter with the latest closing, which it excluded as unverified.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.why: The matter with the latest closing appeared in the agent's own file-name results at [32] and [38] (schedules plus agreements), but it chose the highest-numbered matters to read; the scan at [82] showed it again and the reads at [87] again left it out, so the answer excluded it as unverified.
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) Reviews warned that candidates were picked by matter number and that many surfaced matters were unopened, but never named this matter. The agent listed more matters and ran a scan but never opened it.

other_errors.why: The answer lists older closed deals as qualifying backups beside its chosen matter, beyond the single most recent deal the request asks for.
other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The write review said the comparison candidates could include older or non-qualifying matters that inflate the answer; the check stages kept them.

runs.failure_point: Every file-name pass and its own schedule/closing-evidence table showed the matter with the latest closing, but the agent read candidates by matter number and recency and never opened it.

runs.failure_point: It ranked candidates by matter number from file names, read only the highest-numbered schedule matters, and never opened the matter with the latest closing that its file-name searches listed.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.why: The matter with the latest closing appeared in the agent's own schedule-file and agreement lists at [18]-[21] and [39], but the agent chose the highest-numbered schedule matters to read and never opened it.
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) Reviews warned that candidates were picked by matter number and that many surfaced matters were unopened, but never named this matter. The agent only re-read the two matters it already had.

other_errors.why: The answer offers an older merger as a fallback precedent beside its chosen matter, so two matters are asserted where one most recent deal was asked for.
other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The write review named the fallback precedent as possibly inflating the answer; the check stages left it.

divergence: All fail the same way. Every run's own file-name searches listed the matter with the latest closing among dozens of schedule-bearing matters, and every run chose what to read by matter number or apparent recency, so it was never opened (first error at the first screening stage after it surfaced). Reviews in all runs warned about selection by number and unopened surfaced matters without naming it; T0 and T1 widened their reads after the warnings (T0 even scanned closing dates and saw it) but still left it out, T2 did not widen. Each answer also adds an older fallback or comparison deal, which the write reviews flagged and the agents kept.
